gen-dafont-fenwick-fs-ranade: Ranade moves with a slight, rubbery swell in its stroke. Fenwick is best at holding one width around every turn and filling its bowls, while Ranade does its best work stretching a plain sans line wide and loose.
gen-dafont-fenwick-montserrat: Fenwick, graceful and literary, keeps its line width constant through each turn while its bowls fill out the space. Montserrat then runs on, wide and gliding.
gen-dafont-fenwick-switzer: Switzer reads like thin wire, tubular and tall in the waist. Fenwick does its best work with literary curves that stay open like a horseshoe magnet, while Switzer is best at holding its sans-serif tips apart.
gen-dafont-forza-fs-bespoke-sans: Forza packs its precise, technical letters tight like beads on a wire, with terminals hugging each bowl. Bespoke Sans, by contrast, lets curves breathe away from the stem, so a long passage feels sharp and unhurried.
gen-dafont-forza-fs-neco: Dignified Neco brings a text serif body with a measured swell from hairline to stem, set under a technical heading of rod-stock uniformity. Forza is best at crisp, crowded precision; Neco is best at open authority.
gen-dafont-franchise-roboto-slab: Franchise jams its tall, narrow-stripped letters against one another, with a g drawn in a single unchanging line. Shrink it too far and the crowding bites, while Roboto Slab stays open in its slab-serif middle.
gen-dafont-galaxy-fs-familjen-grotesk: Familjen Grotesk leaves its bowls unfinished on one side and stands tall against its capitals, giving each line a lively lift. Galaxy, with its loose, cosmic spacing, never tires the eye, and neither does the body across a long stretch.
gen-dafont-galaxy-fs-ranade: Slightly rubbery strokes and widely spaced letters give Ranade an organic, unhurried read. Galaxy is best at monoline, commanding drama in a dense tall band; Ranade is best at stretching a sans line out gently.
gen-dafont-galaxy-fs-trench-slab: Galaxy fills the line with cosmic, uninterrupted strokes, tall and loosely fitted like a technical drawing pen. Trench Slab then reads as a dignified serif, its lowercase sitting close to the capitals across a long passage.
gen-dafont-gobold-fs-alpino: Big, bold, and cozy all at once. Gobold is best at geometric curves left open and thick as its stems, while Alpino is best at tall, casual sans-serif letters with stingy spacing.
